requirement_text: The School of Computer Science requires an SAT or an ACT score.
limitations: Live testing-policy page carries no cycle year or 'Fall 20XX' label of its own.
researcher_notes: TRAP CHECK (test-optional/required, top risk for this batch): CMU's testing policy varies by college -- this is real, not uniform. Confirmed independently on 3 separate official CMU properties, all consistent, all currently live as of 2026-08-21: (1) this standardized-testing page; (2) the 'Undergraduate Admission Requirements' page; (3) the course catalog (coursecatalog.web.cmu.edu), which is EXPLICITLY self-dated 'entering in fall 2026' -- i.e. this exact differentiated policy (SCS required / 5 colleges test-flexible / CFA test-optional) was already in force for the Fall 2026 cycle, per the catalog's own words, and remains stated identically on the live undated page retrieved today. Historical origin: CMU provost communication dated 2024-08-29 (https://www.cmu.edu/leadership/the-provost/campus-comms/2024/2024-08-29.html) announced that 'Fall 2025 Applicants' would remain fully test-optional (SCS only 'strongly encouraged' to submit), while 'Fall 2026 Applicants' would move to this differentiated policy -- SCS required, 5 colleges test-flexible, CFA test-optional. That 'strongly encouraged' language does NOT appear anywhere on the current live testing page, confirming the Fall-2025-era language has been fully superseded, not left stale alongside the new policy. Searched specifically for a live stale/pandemic-era (2020-2022) CMU testing page still contradicting this -- none found; the 2024 provost announcement is the only historical document, and it is dated, bound to named past cycles, and does not present itself as current. No CONFLICTING_EVIDENCE found on the testing-policy question itself (contrast with the genuine deadline-date conflict recorded separately in this batch). cycle_year left null per this batch's rule of only setting it when the specific source page names a cycle; the live testing page does not, even though corroborating evidence (catalog, provost announcement) places this exact policy across at least the Fall 2026 and (presumptively) Fall 2027 cycles.

requirement_text: The following colleges and programs operate on a test flexible policy: College of Engineering; Dietrich College of Humanities and Social Sciences; Heinz College's Information Systems program; Mellon College of Science; Tepper School of Business. Test flexible means that students are required to submit test scores in order to complete their application, however, they may choose which type of test(s) they prefer to submit. Acceptable test options include the SAT, ACT, International Baccalaureate (IB) exam (predicted or actual scores), Advanced Placement, Cambridge A-Level (predicted or actual results) and the French Baccalaureate (predicted or actual scores). Students who choose to submit predicted scores/results for the IB exam, Cambridge A-Level or French Baccalaureate will be required to submit their actual scores/results only if they are admitted and choose to enroll.
scope: College of Engineering; Dietrich College of Humanities and Social Sciences; Heinz College's Information Systems program; Mellon College of Science; Tepper School of Business
limitations: 'Required' here means a test score of SOME kind (SAT/ACT/IB/AP/Cambridge A-Level/French Bac) must be submitted -- it is not optional like CFA, but also not narrowly SAT/ACT-only like SCS.
researcher_notes: Program_name left null because this single rule spans 5 named colleges, not one -- see 'scope' field for the exact list. Same undated-page caveat as REQ0001.

requirement_text: The College of Fine Arts is test optional and requires portfolios or auditions.
researcher_notes: Consistent across the standardized-testing page, the undergraduate-admission-requirements page, and the Fall-2026-dated course catalog. CFA is the one college whose testing policy did NOT change in the 2024 provost announcement (it was test-optional before and after).

requirement_text: The College Board no longer offers SAT Subject Tests. These test results are neither required nor recommended, and prior scores won't be considered in our admission process.
researcher_notes: University-wide, applies regardless of which college's testing policy (required/flexible/optional) governs the applicant.

requirement_text: We allow superscoring of SAT test results, but we are unable to accept superscored results for the ACT exam due to the composite score included in the score report.
researcher_notes: NAMED-EXCLUSION-STYLE FACT (category 3 of the scalar-thresholds trap doc): a provenance rule, not a threshold -- an ACT superscore and a single-sitting ACT composite are not interchangeable at CMU even if numerically similar. Corroborated independently on the course catalog page ('we give most weight to the set of scores corresponding to the highest composite score... Carnegie Mellon does not super-score the ACT').

requirement_text: Both domestic and international applicants who submit SAT or ACT scores may share either official or self-reported SAT or ACT scores. Students will not be required to submit official score reports unless they are admitted and choose to enroll. Applicants are able to self-report test scores through the Common Application or by sharing an unofficial score report.
TOEFL iBT or iBT Home Edition. For exams taken before Jan. 21, 2026: We require at least a 102 overall score and give consideration to those with subscores of 25 and above in each section.
limitations: Explicitly bounded to exams taken before 2026-01-21, so unambiguous on its own terms per the same logic that made Edinburgh's pre-cutover TOEFL row unambiguous in the scale audit.
researcher_notes: SCALE TRAP CHECK: date-bounded to the pre-ETS-cutover instrument; both the overall (102) and every subscore (25) are stated on the same legacy 0-120/0-30 scale, so this is fully self-consistent and satisfiable -- not the Glasgow-style mixed-scale defect.

requirement_text: TOEFL iBT or iBT Home Edition. For exams taken on or after Jan. 21, 2026: We require at least a 5 in the overall score and give consideration to those with subscores of 5 and above in each section.
researcher_notes: SCALE TRAP CHECK: unlike the University of Glasgow example in scalar-thresholds-are-not-enough.md (which mixed a comparable-overall figure with an unsatisfiable legacy-scale subtest minimum), CMU's post-cutover requirement states BOTH the overall (5) AND every subscore (5) on the SAME new 1-6 scale -- no mixing of scales, fully satisfiable as published. This is a 'got it right' case like Edinburgh's, not a 'half-satisfiable' case like Glasgow's or Bogazici's.

requirement_text: IELTS (or IELTS Online): We require at least a 7.5 overall band score on the Academic Examination and give consideration to those with subscores of 7.5 and above.
researcher_notes: IELTS's 0-9 band scale is unaffected by the TOEFL rescale (confirmed unaffected in the scale audit).

requirement_text: TOEFL Essentials: We require at least an 11 overall band score and give consideration to those with subscores of 11 and above.
limitations: TOEFL Essentials is a distinct ETS product from TOEFL iBT with its own scale; not affected by the Jan 2026 TOEFL iBT rescale, and no matching enum value exists for it in this batch's test_scale list.

requirement_text: Cambridge English Assessment: We require at least a 191 overall score and give consideration to those with subscores of 191 and above.
researcher_notes: Cambridge English Scale is unaffected by the TOEFL rescale (confirmed unaffected in the scale audit).

requirement_text: Duolingo English Test: we require at least a 135 overall score and give consideration to those with the following subscores and above: Literacy: 135; Conversation: 135; Comprehension: 135; Production: 135.
limitations: Duolingo's native scale (10-160) has no matching enum value in this batch's test_scale list.

requirement_text: Scores should be no more than two years old at the time of application, and we prefer that you submit all English proficiency test results from the past two years.
researcher_notes: RECENCY-RULE-STYLE FACT (category 2 of the scalar-thresholds trap doc): a max-age constraint anchored to 'time of application', distinct from the score threshold itself -- a numerically-qualifying score submitted late is not automatically accepted. No exact anchor date given beyond 'time of application' (contrast CMU's own separate, more precise Mathematics-qualification-style recency rules seen at other universities in this corpus).

requirement_text: Should you take the TOEFL more than once, we'll use the set of TOEFL scores corresponding with your highest overall score. We don't use TOEFL MyBest scores, which 'superscore' subsection results from more than one test administration of the TOEFL.
researcher_notes: NAMED-EXCLUSION-STYLE FACT (category 3 of the trap doc): CMU explicitly rejects TOEFL MyBest superscoring as a provenance, even though a MyBest composite could numerically equal or exceed the 102/5.0 threshold recorded in REQ0007/REQ0008. A threshold-only comparison would wrongly mark a MyBest-sourced score as 'met'.

requirement_text: Recommended English Interviews. InitialView or Vericant interviews are recommended for nonnative English speakers but aren't required. Often these interviews can measure readiness for engagement in the classroom and also showcase a student's personality, likes and dislikes as well as the area of intended major.
limitations: Explicitly optional/recommended, not required -- do not evaluate a missing InitialView/Vericant submission as not_met.

requirement_text: Carnegie Mellon doesn't offer financial aid to international students. If you're an international student who plans to enroll at Carnegie Mellon, you and your family must plan to pay the total cost of attendance.
limitations: Narrow exception exists: see REQ0019 (DACA / specific-country grant eligibility). This is CMU's own general framing for international applicants, not a claim about admission-decision methodology (need-blind vs need-aware) -- see REQ0021 for that separate, unresolved question.
researcher_notes: This is CMU's OWN stated framing, verbatim, and is stronger/more absolute than a typical 'need-aware' policy (which usually implies some aid is available but is a factor for a subset of applicants). CMU's international-applicants page states flatly that no institutional aid exists for this population at all, full stop, rather than describing a need-aware admissions process. Also corroborated by the course catalog: 'Carnegie Mellon doesn't offer financial aid or installment plans to international students.'

requirement_text: It's important for you to use the exact name on your passport on your application, recommendations and test scores. This will eliminate any confusion in the processing of your application.

If your secondary school transcript or any other admission document is written in a language other than English, it should be accompanied by an official translation and verified by a counselor or school official to be true copies of the original.

Only U.S. citizens and permanent residents are eligible for federal and state undergraduate financial aid programs. Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals (DACA) students and a small number of students from specific countries may be eligible for Carnegie Mellon grants.
researcher_notes: Narrows REQ0016's blanket 'no aid to international students' statement: DACA students apply under the international-citizenship-status path per the undergraduate-admission-requirements page ('select "Other (non-US)" as your citizenship status') YET are explicitly aid-eligible via CSS Profile + College Board IDOC -- FAFSA is explicitly NOT required for DACA students. 'A small number of students from specific countries' is not further specified on any page checked in this pass -- left as CMU states it, not expanded.

requirement_text: We're committed to using our aid resources to meet 100% of demonstrated financial need for domestic students, as determined by information on your financial aid application.
researcher_notes: This is a financial-aid GUARANTEE (aid resourcing commitment), not a statement about admission-decision methodology. Corroborated verbatim on the SFS prospective-student aid page ('committed to meeting full demonstrated need') and the SFS undergraduate aid-process page ('committed to meeting the full demonstrated financial need of our domestic students').

requirement_text: No official Carnegie Mellon page checked in this research pass uses the terms 'need-blind,' 'need-aware,' or 'aid-blind' anywhere. Pages checked directly: admission-consideration (holistic-review philosophy page), costs-aid/aid-affordability, sfs.cmu.edu undergraduate financial-aid process page (both prospective- and returning-student versions), and the international-applicants page. None state whether ability to pay or demonstrated financial need is a factor in the admission decision itself, for either domestic or international applicants.
scope: admission-decision methodology re: financial need, specifically
limitations: This record documents an absence, not a policy value. Do not infer need-blind OR need-aware from CMU's silence; do not infer it from the domestic full-need-met aid GUARANTEE (REQ0020) either, since a meets-full-need aid commitment does not by itself establish whether need is considered during admission review.
researcher_notes: CORRECTION TO RESEARCH BRIEF: the task brief anticipated 'CMU is need-aware for a meaningful share of applicants (especially international) rather than fully need-blind' and asked this be verified rather than assumed. A general web search surfaced third-party (non-CMU, non-official) claims that CMU has an 'aid-blind' / 'need-blind' domestic admissions policy, but that exact phrase does not appear on any official cmu.edu page fetched directly in this pass (confirmed by both a raw-HTML grep for 'need-blind'/'need-aware'/'aid-blind' on the costs-aid and sfs.cmu.edu pages, and by asking each page directly). What IS confirmed from CMU's own pages: (1) domestic students get a 100%-demonstrated-need-met AID commitment (REQ0020); (2) international students get essentially no institutional aid at all, narrow DACA/specific-country exception aside (REQ0016, REQ0019). Neither fact resolves whether financial need is weighed IN the admission decision itself. Recording as an explicit, verified 'unknown' per this lane's evidence rule 6 ('unknown is a valid result') rather than repeating an unverified secondary-source claim as if it were CMU's own statement.

requirement_text: Early Decision is a binding application plan. If you're admitted to Carnegie Mellon, you're expected to enroll. You should not apply for Early Decision if you have a pending Early Decision application with another college or university. If admitted through Early Decision, you must agree to withdraw applications previously submitted to other institutions. To do this, please complete and submit the Early Decision Agreement (PDF) along with the rest of your application. Because Early Decision is binding, you won't be able to compare financial aid offers between institutions. ... Three decisions can be given: admit, deny or defer to Regular Decision. You're not able to reapply under Regular Decision if you're denied under Early Decision.
researcher_notes: This is a binding contractual commitment, not a checkable eligibility fact -- should not be auto-converted into a structured_rule threshold by a future interpretation pass; needs human review to represent correctly. Additional mechanics from the course catalog (a second, independent official source, corroborating): 'Applying Early Decision won't affect your overall admission decision. Students applying Early and Regular Decision are admitted at almost exactly the same rate.' The only stated release valve from the binding agreement, per the Early Decision Agreement PDF referenced on this page (PDF itself not fetched in this pass -- flagged, not guessed), is not detailed on the HTML page itself; unlike Columbia's equivalent page (wave 1, REQ-2026-08-21-COL0028) which explicitly names 'financial reasons' as the sole release valve, CMU's HTML page does not spell out the release condition in the text actually fetched here -- recorded as a genuine gap rather than assumed to match Columbia's.

requirement_text: Carnegie Mellon offers only one binding Early Decision round for first-year applicants (deadline in early November). No 'Early Decision II' round exists. The official Application Plans & Deadlines page and the course catalog's 'Application Plans' section each enumerate exactly two first-year plans -- Early Decision and Regular Decision -- with no second early round. The university's own Common Data Set 2025-2026 (Section C21) has a dedicated field for 'Other early decision plan closing date' (i.e., an ED II slot) and CMU left it BLANK.
researcher_notes: CORRECTION TO RESEARCH BRIEF: the task brief asked to verify both Early Decision and 'possibly ED II' rather than assume both exist -- confirmed, by direct evidence, that CMU does NOT offer ED II. Cross-checked 3 independent official sources: (1) live Application Plans & Deadlines page -- 'ED' and 'RD' only, zero occurrences of 'ED II' or 'Early Decision II' in the raw fetched HTML; (2) course catalog's Application Plans section -- same two-plan structure; (3) Common Data Set 2025-2026 C21, which has an explicit structured field for a second/'other' early decision plan and CMU's own submission leaves it empty -- the strongest single piece of evidence, since it is a structured yes/blank field CMU fills out itself rather than marketing copy. This matches the pattern the wave-1 Columbia agent found (REQ-2026-08-21-COL0029): third-party admissions-consulting sites claim an 'ED II' round exists at CMU with a January deadline, but that figure is identical to CMU's separately and officially published Regular Decision deadline -- those secondary sources most likely mislabel Regular Decision as 'ED II', or conflate CMU with a peer institution that genuinely offers split ED I/II rounds. No ED II deadline or requirement record created.

requirement_text: Early Decision is not available for acting, directing, dramaturgy, music theater, BXA Design programs or the School of Music. [Separately, in the catalog's BXA section:] BXA options aren't available for those applying to the School of Drama, or for external transfer applicants. Under Early Decision, BXA is only available for the Schools of Architecture and Art.
limitations: Sourced from the course catalog, which is explicitly self-dated to the Fall 2026 entry cycle (now closed as of this 2026-08-21 retrieval date -- Fall 2026 matriculation has already begun). Two verbatim sentences from two different sections of the same catalog page are merged here (bracketed note marks the join) -- hence extracted_summary, not verbatim_quoted. The exclusion list itself (Drama sub-programs / Music / BXA Design) is corroborated on the live, undated Application Plans & Deadlines page in the shorter form 'Early Decision is not available for the School of Drama, BXA Design programs or the School of Music,' so the EXCLUSION RULE is high-confidence current; only the specific cycle-year binding of this exact catalog wording is historical.
researcher_notes: The BXA nuance ('BXA is only available for the Schools of Architecture and Art' under ED) appears only in the course catalog's fuller text, not on the shorter live deadlines page -- i.e. BXA+Design and BXA+Music are excluded from ED (consistent with Design and Music both being excluded generally), while BXA+Architecture and BXA+Art ARE ED-eligible. BXA is not offered at all with the School of Drama (unconditionally, not just for ED).

requirement_text: Required Application Materials for Undergraduate Admission: Common Application; $75 Application Fee* ... *Carnegie Mellon accepts fee waivers from students who meet one of the indicators of economic need as outlined on the Common Application.
Required Application Materials for Undergraduate Admission includes: Secondary School Counselor Evaluation; Teacher Recommendation.
researcher_notes: Exactly one teacher recommendation and one counselor evaluation -- not a range. Per the course catalog, the teacher recommendation must be 'submitted to the Office of Admission by November 3 for Early Decision and by January 15 for Regular Decision' (see companion deadline records).

requirement_text: Common Application Essay. Common Application Writing Supplement -- This includes three short-answer questions.
limitations: Exact prompt wording for the three short-answer questions was NOT found on any official cmu.edu page fetched in this pass -- only the count and format ('three short-answer questions') are confirmed verbatim from an official source. Numerous third-party college-admissions-consulting sites publish specific prompt text, but per this lane's evidence rule 1 (official sources only, no admissions-consulting sites), that text was NOT recorded here since it could not be verified against an official CMU or Common App page directly.
researcher_notes: Prompts are administered through the Common Application platform itself (commonapp.org), which was not separately fetched in this pass; a future pass could verify exact wording directly against the Common App's own official CMU-specific supplement page.

requirement_text: Carnegie Mellon doesn't accept supplemental submissions, such as resumes, artwork, portfolios, recording or websites. We encourage you to use the Common Application, along with the Carnegie Mellon Supplemental Essays, to highlight experiences or activities that have enhanced or defined your personal growth during high school.
limitations: This is the GENERAL rule for applicants outside the College of Fine Arts. It does not override CFA's own required portfolio/pre-screening/audition process (see the School of Architecture / Art / Design / Drama / Music records), nor the optional Schoolhouse.world exception (REQ0029).

requirement_text: As part of our partnership with Khan Academy, Carnegie Mellon will consider a Schoolhouse.world portfolio as part of its holistic undergraduate admissions review process. ... While Schoolhouse.world certifications do not replace official application materials like transcripts or letters of recommendation, they can help improve your application.
limitations: Explicitly optional/supplementary, not required.

requirement_text: Relative importance of 'Interview' in first-time, first-year, degree-seeking admission decisions: Not considered.
limitations: This is CMU's own aggregate, university-wide Common Data Set answer. It is contradicted at the individual-program level by the School of Drama's Design/Production track, which requires an interview as 'the main basis of your admission decision' (see the College of Fine Arts records), and by the School of Music's Electronic Music concentration, which requires a faculty interview. The CDS's own instructions direct 'Please provide additional information if the importance of any specific academic or nonacademic factors differ by academic program' and CMU's answer there is only a generic pointer to the admissions website, not a call-out of the Drama/Music exceptions.
researcher_notes: 'Not considered' at the CDS aggregate level should not be read as blocking Drama Design/Production or Music Electronic Music applicants' required interviews from being evaluated.

requirement_text: College of Engineering: 4 years English; 4 years Mathematics* (should include at least algebra, geometry, trigonometry, analytic geometry, elementary functions (pre-calculus) and preferably calculus; advanced mathematics courses are strongly encouraged, especially a course in calculus); 1 year Chemistry; 1 year Physics; 1 year Biology; 2 years Foreign Language; 3 Electives.

College of Fine Arts -- School of Architecture: 4 years Mathematics* (should include at least algebra, geometry, trigonometry, analytic geometry, elementary functions as well as pre-calculus; advanced mathematics courses are encouraged); 1 year Physics; 2 years Foreign Language; 5 Electives.
limitations: No explicit English-coursework line item is listed for Architecture on this page, unlike every other college/school listed (all of which state '4 years English' explicitly). Recorded exactly as published rather than assuming a 4-year English requirement by analogy to other colleges.

requirement_text: College of Fine Arts -- School of Design: 4 years English; 2 years Mathematics; 2 years Science; 2 years Foreign Language; 6 Electives.
College of Fine Arts -- School of Drama: 4 years English; 10 Electives.
limitations: No mathematics, science, or foreign-language coursework line item is listed for Drama on this page -- recorded exactly as published, not assumed.

requirement_text: College of Fine Arts -- School of Music: 4 years English; 2 years Foreign Language; 10 Electives.
limitations: No mathematics or science coursework line item is listed for Music on this page -- recorded exactly as published, not assumed.

requirement_text: College of Fine Arts -- School of Art: 4 years English; 10 Electives.
limitations: No mathematics, science, or foreign-language coursework line item is listed for Art on this page -- recorded exactly as published, not assumed.

program_name: Dietrich College of Humanities and Social Sciences
requirement_text: Dietrich College of Humanities and Social Sciences: 4 years English; 3 years Mathematics* (should include at least algebra, geometry, trigonometry, analytic geometry, elementary functions as well as pre-calculus for those pursuing Bachelor of Arts degree programs; advanced mathematics courses are strongly encouraged for those pursuing Bachelor of Science degree programs); 1 year Science (2 years or more preferred); 2 years Foreign Language; 6 Electives.
researcher_notes: Dietrich has its own internal BA/BS split on the math recommendation -- 3 years is the required floor for both, but BS-track applicants are specifically steered toward more advanced math than the BA floor implies.

requirement_text: Information Systems: 4 years English; 4 years Mathematics* (should include at least algebra, geometry, trigonometry, analytic geometry, elementary functions (pre-calculus) and preferably calculus; advanced mathematics courses are encouraged, especially a course in calculus); 1 year Science (2 years or more preferred); 2 years Foreign Language; 6 Electives.
researcher_notes: Information Systems sits administratively under Heinz College for the testing-flexible policy (REQ0002) but is listed as its own line item, separate from Dietrich College, on the academic-requirements page.

requirement_text: Mellon College of Science: 4 years English; 4 years Mathematics* (should include at least algebra, geometry, trigonometry, analytic geometry, elementary functions (pre-calculus) and preferably calculus; advanced mathematics courses are strongly encouraged, especially a course in calculus); 1 year Chemistry; 1 year Physics; 1 year Biology; 2 years Foreign Language; 3 Electives.

School of Computer Science: 4 years English; 4 years Mathematics* (should include at least algebra, geometry, trigonometry, analytic geometry, elementary functions (pre-calculus) and preferably calculus; advanced mathematics courses are strongly encouraged, especially a course in calculus); 1 year Physics; 2 years of Chemistry, Biology or Computer Science; 2 years Foreign Language; 3 Electives.
researcher_notes: SCS is the only college whose science requirement is stated as a flexible 2-of-3 menu ('2 years of Chemistry, Biology or Computer Science') rather than fixed 1-year blocks in specific named sciences -- a genuine, distinctive per-college difference, not a copy-paste variant of the Engineering/MCS/Tepper pattern.

requirement_text: Tepper School of Business: 4 years English; 4 years Mathematics* (should include at least algebra, geometry, trigonometry, analytic geometry, elementary functions (pre-calculus) and preferably calculus; advanced mathematics courses are encouraged, especially a course in calculus); 1 year Chemistry; 1 year Physics; 1 year Biology; 2 years Foreign Language; 3 Electives.

Carnegie Mellon may grant advanced placement and credit for scores of four and five on exams taken in the Advanced Placement program. ... Each college or school within Carnegie Mellon creates their own curriculum and thus decides how AP or IB exams contribute toward your degree.
limitations: This is a credit/placement policy, not an admission eligibility threshold -- do not evaluate as an admission requirement.

requirement_text: Carnegie Mellon also recognizes the International Baccalaureate examinations and may grant advanced standing and/or credit in various fields for scores of six or seven on the higher level exams.
limitations: Credit/placement policy, not an admission eligibility threshold.

requirement_text: Carnegie Mellon recognizes the Cambridge GCE A-Level (advanced level) examinations in various higher-level subjects and may grant advanced placement and/or credit for exemplary grades. ... Please note that we do not accept GCE "O" level examinations for placement.
researcher_notes: NAMED-EXCLUSION-STYLE FACT: GCE O-level explicitly and permanently excluded from placement/credit consideration, regardless of grade -- distinct from A-Level's exam-taking role as a valid test-flexible submission option under REQ0002.

requirement_text: If you're applying to the School of Architecture, you must submit a portfolio of 10 creative works that showcases evidence of your curiosity, critical thinking, innovation, problem-solving, spatial reasoning/visual thinking, ability to synthesize and desire to make and build things.

If you're applying to the School of Art, you must submit a portfolio of 10 to 20 recent creative works that showcase both your imagination and technical skills. We recommend including as many works as possible that were completed independently and outside of the classroom.
If you're applying to the School of Design, you must submit a portfolio of up to 18 slides in addition to a two-minute video introducing yourself to the Design faculty reviewing your portfolio.

All Drama applicants must apply to Carnegie Mellon through the Common Application and submit a separate School of Drama application through Acceptd by the posted deadline. The School of Drama does not consider applicants for Early Decision.
researcher_notes: Drama uses a second, distinct application platform (Acceptd) alongside the Common Application -- not simply an upload to the Common App itself.

requirement_text: Acting/Music Theater: Applicants should apply and complete the pre-screening process by December 1. If selected from the pre-screening process, you'll be contacted to schedule an audition, which is the main basis of your admission decision.

Design/Production: Applicants should apply and submit their portfolio by December 1. If selected from the pre-screening process, you'll be contacted to schedule an interview, which is the main basis of your admission decision.
researcher_notes: Directly contradicts the university-wide CDS 'Interview: Not Considered' aggregate (REQ0030) at the individual-program level -- for this specific track, an interview is stated to be THE main basis of the admission decision, not merely one input among many.

requirement_text: Dramaturgy: Applicants should apply and submit their additional materials by December 1. Additional application materials include: A resume; A brief (less than 750 word) letter that addresses the question: "Why are you interested in studying dramaturgy, and what experience do you bring to the area of study?"; Two (2) letters of recommendation from sources familiar with your research and writing skills; Two (2) samples of original argumentative writing that are approximately 1,000 words each.
researcher_notes: Dramaturgy's 2 recommendation letters are IN ADDITION TO, and a different kind of letter than, the university-wide 1 teacher recommendation + 1 counselor evaluation (REQ0026) -- these are specifically framed as attesting to 'research and writing skills'.

requirement_text: All Music applicants must apply to Carnegie Mellon through the Common Application and submit a separate School of Music application by the posted deadline. Regular Decision: Apply and submit your School of Music application, including portfolio and pre-screening materials, by December 1. Live auditions will take place in February. The School of Music does not consider applicants for Early Decision.

If you're applying for Composition, you'll be required to submit a portfolio composed of three (3) manuscripts of original compositions showing your range in genre, training and ability as well as an audio recording of each of the submitted compositions.

If you're applying for Electronic Music, you'll need to submit a portfolio containing samples of your creative work, providing documentation of your electronic music making in the form of high-quality sound and video recordings. Additionally, you'll be required to schedule an interview with Electronic Music faculty. The School of Music will reach out in January to schedule that interview where applicable.
researcher_notes: A second, distinct required-interview track alongside Drama Design/Production (REQ0050) -- both contradict the university-wide CDS 'Interview: Not Considered' aggregate at the individual-program level.

requirement_text: Note that BXA applicants are only reviewed for the College of Fine Arts (CFA). If you indicate interest in the BXA program, you will not be reviewed for a second college/program outside of your CFA choice. ... Students must meet the admission standards of their academic choice and complete the specific application requirements for their CFA focus (portfolio review, pre-screen, audition or interview).

Admission to the Schools of Drama and Music is based primarily on a pre-screen, audition or (for select School of Music programs) portfolio review. Applicants to the Schools of Architecture, Art and Design will be evaluated not only on the basis of their portfolio review but also on their academic performance. Applicants to the College of Engineering, Mellon College of Science, School of Computer Science and Tepper School of Business will be evaluated on their academic performance, with emphasis on strength in mathematics and science. Applicants to the Dietrich College of Humanities and Social Sciences and the Information Systems program will be evaluated on their academic performance, with emphasis on reading and comprehension abilities along with mathematics coursework. We'll also evaluate both groups of applicants based on their ability to communicate thoughts and ideas in writing.
limitations: Sourced from the Fall-2026-dated course catalog. This is a description of evaluative EMPHASIS, not a pass/fail eligibility rule, and is unlikely to be a fact that changes cycle-to-cycle -- recorded as historical per this batch's strict dating discipline, but likely still descriptive of current practice.
researcher_notes: Confirms real, substantive per-college variation in HOW applicants are evaluated, not just what documents are required -- the clearest single statement found of CMU's genuinely different admission processes per college, as anticipated by the research brief.

requirement_text: You may apply to up to two colleges/programs if your second choice program is from the College of Fine Arts -- you cannot apply to more than one academic program. (Early Decision and transfer candidates may only apply to one college/program.)
limitations: Sourced from the Fall-2026-dated course catalog; corroborated in substance by the live Admission Consideration/Requirements pages describing single-college review, though the exact 'up to two, second must be CFA' phrasing was found verbatim only in the catalog.

requirement_text: If admitted, you must provide proof of meeting all requirements for an official high school diploma by the end of May of the year of graduation. You must also submit an official final transcript, GED or certificate of completion from your local school district or state board of education by the end of July of the year of matriculation.
The Where Am I in the Process? portal service is intended for individuals at least 13 years old; if you intend to apply and are not at least 13, please contact the Office of Admission.
